data.description:
Goal:
Real apps need 5-50 secrets at startup, not one. Today Thimble has
`render` (emits to stdout, operator wrangles a file or env) and
`and-get` (one secret to stdin). The middle ground — "hand the whole
namespace to my app at startup without touching a filesystem" — is
missing. Add `thimble exec` to fork+exec a child with the entire
decrypted namespace either piped as dotenv on stdin (default) or
populated in the child's env block (`--env`).

This is the realistic operator pattern for systemd / Docker / bare
metal deploy, and it strictly improves on the common "render to
/run/x.env then EnvironmentFile=" because no file is ever created
on the deploy host.

Verification:
1. New subcommand `thimble exec <app> <env> -- <command> [args...]`.
2. Default (no flag): decrypt the namespace; fork+exec command; pipe
   dotenv-encoded body to the child's stdin; close stdin; wait;
   exit with the child's exit code. No file on the deploy host at
   any point. Same pipe + dup2 pattern as `and-get`.
3. `--env` flag: decrypt the namespace; fork+exec command with each
   key=value injected into the child's env block; do NOT also write
   to stdin. No file at any point.
4. Refusal: `--env` together with a child whose basename is a shell
   (sh/bash/zsh/fish/pwsh/cmd.exe/powershell) or a docker/podman
   command without `--env-file=-` reuses K-24's shell-guard logic
   and is rejected unless `--allow-shell-env` is also passed.
5. Refusal: passing the secret values as positional args after
   `<command>` is impossible — there's no flag/path that surfaces
   values into argv. Tests prove this.
6. Audit log gains an `exec` op (audit/audit.go) so operators can
   tell when a namespace was decrypted for an app start.
7. README's "Consuming Secrets From Your App" subsection (new) walks
   through stdin-flavor and env-flavor with concrete code in Go,
   Python, Node, Ruby. Trade-off table is honest about env-block
   leakage via /proc.
8. Tests: stdin flavor delivers a parseable dotenv string covering
   all keys; env flavor sets exactly the namespace keys plus parent
   env, no extras; child exit code propagates; secrets never appear
   in argv (assert via /proc/$child/cmdline read in a subprocess).
9. Integration test against real `age`: real bundle, real exec, real
   environ inspection.

Constraints:
- Knot ref: K-58; depends on K-24 (shell guard reused) and K-23
  (stderr suppression patterns).
- Files: internal/cli/run_exec.go (new), internal/cli/run_exec_test.go,
  internal/cli/io.go (extend runSecretConsumer or add a sibling),
  internal/audit/audit.go (new op), README.md, SECURITY.md threat
  model row updated.
- Reuses K-24's shell-guard verbatim — same blacklist, same
  `--allow-shell-env` escape hatch.
- The dotenv emitted to the child's stdin uses the existing
  `internal/dotenv` encoder; no new format.
- Public CLI surface: `thimble exec <app> <env> -- <cmd> [args...]`
  with optional `--env`, `--allow-shell-env`. Update printUsage and
  the README "Everyday CLI" section.
- Signal handling: SIGINT/SIGTERM to thimble forwards to the child
  (via the existing cli.Run context); secret in pipe buffer is
  freed when thimble exits.
- The `--env` flavor must NOT also write to stdin. Operators who
  want both can pipe explicitly. Default (no flag) = stdin only.
